**8B.2 Research Note**
Assessment: mostly yes, but uneven. Marcos did translate the 2024 program into a real set of priorities, plans, institutions, appointments, timelines, and enforcement steps. The strongest evidence is in executive orders, the SONA, procurement reform, security/cyber roadmaps, social-protection expansions, and anti-rent actions. The main caveat is that implementation was mixed: some flagship measures were only partly effective, and some institutions still concentrated discretion in the presidency.

**Supports**
- [SONA highlights whole-of-government effort to achieve food security, inclusive economic growth - NEDA](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/sona-highlights-whole-of-government-effort-to-achieve-food-security-inclusive-economic-growth-neda/) | Presidential Communications Office / NEDA | 2024-07-23 | Claim: The administration explicitly linked the SONA to implementing the `Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028`, giving the program a formal planning framework and policy sequence. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.1, 7B.5
- [3rd State of the Nation Address of His Excellency Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.](https://stateofthenation.gov.ph/sona/2024/) | Office of the President | 2024-07-22 | Claim: The speech named concrete priorities such as rice-price stabilization, agriculture support, anti-poverty measures, flood control, and education/technology upgrades, showing a revealed implementation agenda. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.1, 7B.5
- [PBBM orders Pag-Abot institutionalized for street dwellers and vulnerable people](https://mirror.pia.gov.ph/press-releases/2024/01/22/pbbm-issues-eo-no-52-institutionalizing-and-expanding-dswds-pag-abot-program-for-street-dwellers-other-poor-and-vulnerable-individuals) | Presidential Communications Office via PIA | 2024-01-22 | Claim: EO 52 created an inter-agency committee, monitoring system, and biannual reporting for Pag-Abot, which is clear evidence of converting a social program into a standing institution. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [PBBM adopts DICT's National Cybersecurity Plan 2023-2028](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-adopts-dicts-national-cybersecurity-plan-2023-2028/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-06 | Claim: EO 58 turned the cybersecurity plan into a whole-of-nation roadmap and required agencies and LGUs to implement and report on it, which is a real implementation mechanism. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.8, 7B.9
- [PBBM approves National Cybersecurity Plan to fortify PH against various threats](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-approves-national-cybersecurity-plan-to-fortify-ph-against-various-threats/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-02-08 | Claim: The plan was described as policy direction with operational guidelines and stakeholder consultation, indicating the administration moved from slogan to a documented policy architecture. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.1, 7B.8
- [PBBM signs laws on streamlining procurement, combatting online scams](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-20 | Claim: The procurement law standardized forms and institutionalized e-procurement, directly reducing discretion and creating a concrete anti-favoritism enforcement mechanism. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [PBBM orders agencies to help COS, JO workers get permanent positions in government](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-agencies-to-help-cos-jo-workers-get-permanent-positions-in-government/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-25 | Claim: Marcos directed agencies to regularize long-serving workers through training and eligibility, which translates staffing priorities into a concrete administrative process. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.9
- [PBBM orders activation of online platform to monitor El Niño, La Niña phenomena](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-activation-of-online-platform-to-monitor-el-nino-la-nina-phenomena/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-03-26 | Claim: Marcos ordered a public dashboard with sector conditions, interventions, and citizen reporting, which is concrete monitoring infrastructure rather than rhetoric. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.10, 7B.5
- [PBBM orders 4Ps expansion to cover pregnant, lactating women](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-4ps-expansion-to-cover-pregnant-lactating-women-to-ensure-childrens-health-well-being-in-first-1000-days/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-06-11 | Claim: The cash-transfer expansion targeted maternal-child health and nutrition, showing a concrete priority translated into a specific program change. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [PBBM fores special interventions for PWDs](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-fosters-pwd-friendly-philippines/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-23 | Claim: Marcos announced PWD interventions and PhilHealth benefits for PWD children and senior citizens, which is a concrete social-policy implementation step. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [PBBM inks law to further boost PH rice industry](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-inks-law-to-further-boost-ph-rice-industry/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-12-09 | Claim: Extending and enlarging RCEF operationalized the rice agenda through a structural farm-support law, not just a promise. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.5, 7B.9
- [PBBM refutes alleged loophole in EO 74, reiterates POGO ban in all forms](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-refutes-alleged-loophole-in-eo-74-reiterates-pogo-ban-in-all-forms/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-11-11 | Claim: Marcos clarified that the POGO ban covered related licenses and loopholes, showing enforcement follow-through rather than symbolic rhetoric. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.9, 7B.10

**Counters**
- [NEDA said EO 62 did not lower retail rice prices as anticipated](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/929579/neda-reduced-rice-tariffs-failed-to-lower-prices/story/) | GMA News Online | 2024-12-10 | Claim: The flagship rice intervention had only partial success, showing that some translated priorities did not reliably convert into outcomes. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.5, 7B.10
- [Philippines says had frank, candid talks with China on South China Sea](https://www.theprint.in/world/philippines-says-had-frank-candid-talks-with-china-on-south-china-sea/2263722/) | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-09-12 | Claim: Dialogue and hotline mechanisms continued, but the record still shows a work-in-progress rather than a completed implementation system. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.1
- [Marcos reorganized the National Security Council](https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_81_2024.html) | Lawphil / Office of the President | 2024-12-30 | Claim: EO 81 institutionalized coordination, but it also preserved strong presidential discretion to appoint additional members, so the mechanism is real but centralized. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.9, 8B.1
- [Freedom House: Philippines - Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: Politics remained shaped by patronage, weak campaign-finance rules, and kinship, which implies some of the operating environment stayed transactional despite formal program translation. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism: Philippines](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | Claim: Red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and regulatory pressure persisted, showing that implementation and institutional safeguards were incomplete in practice. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [Marcos’s economic reforms improved lives in 2024](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbms-economic-reforms-improved-lives-in-2024/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-12-31 | Claim: The administration’s own year-end wrapup highlights liberalization, privatization, and globalization, but it is self-reporting and does not by itself prove execution quality. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.1

**Search gap**
- I did not find a single integrated public implementation matrix that ties every 2024 promise to a funded budget line, deadline, owner, and enforcement metric in one place.
- The evidence is strongest where Marcos used EO, law, or formal agency process. It is weaker where the record depends on speeches, sector briefings, or Palace self-assessment.
- The largest unresolved gap is independent verification of how consistently the translated priorities were funded and enforced across the whole bureaucracy.
